text: A price feed's signal had no age check, so a stale signal could be used. An adversarial review agent found it, beyond its brief.
One cell of a price replay looked strong. Pre-registered robustness checks (a shifted clock, a calendar split) refused it in the same build.
An agent challenged a closed verdict by mixing up the smallest effect a test can detect with its interval. Recomputing from the committed table rejected the challenge.
An idea was labelled established on the premise that new listings had no quotes. The next research loop found that almost all already had them.
A replay's large gain came from look-ahead. A decomposition rule flagged it in the same commit.
A positive secondary cell did not replicate when it was tested as the pre-registered primary on a set of related markets.
A result chosen on the same data failed its frozen holdout. The claim then stayed in the project's main notes for a month after the failure was recorded.
A candidate from a first look was closed by its registered second look. A weak row: a test doing its job, not an agent mistake.
A comparison script had a logic bug. An independent review marked it a blocker.
A draft public thread made two false claims, one about how long the work had run. A reader agent flagged that one the day it appeared; a trace of each claim to its file and line corrected both.
An audit program gave the wrong reason flag on a look-ahead case. The independent checker's first run caught it.
A draft said the audit's rulebook was time-stamped on a blockchain. On that date it was only frozen in git and pushed. A copy-draft agent caught the orchestrator's error.
An eval rubric asked for a cause the task gave no way to find. Blind grading of the rerun showed it.
A commit deleted 226 lines of safety code. A halt during a paper-mode soak test led to the investigation that found it; the stripped code never ran.

The paper trader filled every order at once at its limit price and charged no fees. I noticed a balance gap in a live run and stopped the bot. A collaborator, not an agent, wrote the instant fills; the agents kept the model for two months.
A new bot's scanner used the settlement time as the order deadline, so none of its live orders filled.
A price filter fell back to a stale setting and silently rejected markets in a live bot.
A bot went live on a signal that did not match its backtest. An ad hoc check found it, and that check became a launch rule.
Six code pushes caused six restarts during a live run. I asked for every fix in one batch.
The notes held a wrong rule about when trading closes before settlement. A later sprint found it while reproducing the settlement rule, which matched every case.
A figure in the notes was cited to a document that does not contain it. A sweep that re-derived cited numbers found it.
A backtest had look-ahead, and a bot had gone live on it. A re-analysis found it. The source lists it twice; it is counted once.
An agent diagnosed a stuck bot without tracing the code. I made it trace the code mechanically; that found the real cause, about an hour in.
An incident report overstated how much of the logs it covered. I challenged the report as vague, and the agent disclosed the overstatement.
A new background loop was not stubbed in the tests, so CI hung on every pull request until a fix 14 days later.
A stale headline figure stayed in the notes. Rerunning the canonical report found it.
The notes said no events reached a price band. Re-deriving from the raw file showed that some did.
An agent re-ran a test that an earlier verdict had already closed, without checking the notes first. I caught it. It cost about 39 minutes and 144k tokens.
A web research agent's stale report of a product launch was relayed to me as news. The sources do not say who noticed.
A per-trade figure was quoted from a scan that had not finished. A quant review's question led to a reread of the full scan.
A reported match rate was a floating-point artifact, and a results table could not be reproduced. An adversarial review caught both.
Two agents gave two numbers for one measure, 99.09% and 93.91%, one of them from a filter nobody declared. Result tables with declared filters caught it.
A replay measured the bot's own resting order instead of the market, so its result was an artifact. An adversarial review led to its withdrawal the same day.
A safety-check skill looked for code names that never existed in the code. A prompt audit found it.
A script kept the label 'canonical, look-ahead fixed' after a second look-ahead was found in it. A sweep found the stale label.
The notes miscounted how many liquid series existed. A census found more, and several of them listed nothing.
A file pattern picked a metadata file as the data file. A sweep of every such pattern found it.
A cost was ported from another market instead of measured. Measuring each market's own depth showed the port was wrong.
A results file that must never change was edited by hand after it was built. An audit re-run found it.
A data pull rewrote a raw file in place when it resumed. The same audit re-run found it.
Five result tables were built from inputs kept in a temporary session folder, so they cannot be rebuilt.
Some verify steps wrote the file before comparing, and others compared nothing, while the notes said every check matched byte for byte.
A fill test used a five-minute window and called markets too small. The lead withdrew the rule and reran with a 24-hour window.

The notes contradicted the code, and a skill cited sources that did not exist. A prompt audit with 155 findings; several defects in one row, with no single start date.
Figures copied by hand into the notes did not match their table. A data review found them.
The notes kept saying a script had a hard-coded value after a fix the same day had removed it.
A push carried four commits from another session along with its own. The pushing session listed them and told me. Private repo only.
A missed recording lost rows from a paper ledger.
A scheduled dry run did not start.

A move list overstated how a holdout failed: the point estimate came out ahead, and only the lower bound fell short. A claims review caught it.
